study: pattern loading on a continuous steel girder
title: LESS LIVE LOAD NEXT DOOR, MORE SAG HERE
claim: In the registered rigid, level, equal-span linear-elastic continuous-girder models, the governing live-load pattern loaded the target end bay and every second bay from it. The largest end-bay sag was 1.39 to 1.76 times the all-bays-loaded sag; permanent load reduces the ratio, and flexible supports can shrink or reverse the effect.

identity: WORKER DRAWN TO SCALE, 1.70 m - AN ILLUSTRATION
what_is_not_claimed: Linear elastic, small displacement, quasi-static load cases: removing the load is not a dynamic event. A 2-D beam with rigid, level supports and equal spans in the core; flexible supports can shrink or reverse the effect, and permanent load on every span reduces the ratio. Deflection, not strength: with every bay loaded the interior support moment governs first yield. No slab, composite action, connection or column flexibility. Interior spans are not quoted: their all-bays sag is small enough that their ratio is not a comparable number.
verification_not_validation: The two-span coefficients and the support moment are reproduced from beam theory, the ratios do not move between 48 and 96 elements per span, and every live-load subset is enumerated. All of it reads the same idealisation the solver reads. No measured girder is reproduced here.
